|   |       `-- ReadThread delivers output to Termio.processOutput()

|   |           `-- Windows: one read loop reads and processes output

|   |       `-- StreamHandler.vt() / vtPrintAscii() dispatch terminal operations

|   `-- StreamHandler bridges effects outside the grid (src/termio/stream_handler.zig)
|       |-- Terminal queries -> termio_mailbox -> reply bytes to the child
|       |-- Titles, bells, clipboard requests -> surface_mailbox -> runtime handling
|       `-- queueRender() / renderer_mailbox -> renderer wakeup and presentation updates

|   |-- Wakeup -> drainMailbox() -> renderCallback() -> Renderer.updateFrame()
|   |-- Renderer = GenericRenderer(GraphicsAPI) (src/renderer.zig)

1	//! Surface represents a single terminal "surface". A terminal surface is
     2	//! a minimal "widget" where the terminal is drawn and responds to events
     3	//! such as keyboard and mouse. Each surface also creates and owns its pty
     4	//! session.
     5	//!
     6	//! The word "surface" is used because it is left to the higher level
     7	//! application runtime to determine if the surface is a window, a tab,
     8	//! a split, a preview pane in a larger window, etc. This struct doesn't care:
     9	//! it just draws and responds to events. The events come from the application
    10	//! runtime so the runtime can determine when and how those are delivered
    11	//! (i.e. with focus, without focus, and so on).
    12	const Surface = @This();
    13	
    14	const apprt = @import("apprt.zig");
    15	pub const Mailbox = apprt.surface.Mailbox;
    16	pub const Message = apprt.surface.Message;
    17	
    18	const std = @import("std");
    19	const builtin = @import("builtin");
    20	const assert = @import("quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    21	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    22	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    23	const global = @import("global.zig");
    24	const oni = @import("oniguruma");
    25	const simd = @import("simd/main.zig");
    26	const crash = @import("crash/main.zig");
    27	const unicode = @import("unicode/main.zig");
    28	const rendererpkg = @import("renderer.zig");
    29	const termio = @import("termio.zig");
    30	const font = @import("font/main.zig");
    31	const Command = @import("Command.zig");
    32	const terminal = @import("terminal/main.zig");
    33	const configpkg = @import("config.zig");
    34	const Duration = configpkg.Config.Duration;
    35	const input = @import("input.zig");
    36	const App = @import("App.zig");
    37	const internal_os = @import("os/main.zig");
    38	const inspectorpkg = @import("inspector/main.zig");
    39	const SurfaceMouse = @import("surface_mouse.zig");
    40	const ProcessInfo = @import("pty.zig").ProcessInfo;
    41	
    42	const log = std.log.scoped(.surface);
    43	
    44	// The renderer implementation to use.
    45	const Renderer = rendererpkg.Renderer;
    46	
    47	/// Minimum window size in cells. This is used to prevent the window from
    48	/// being resized to a size that is too small to be useful. These defaults
    49	/// are chosen to match the default size of Mac's Terminal.app, but is
    50	/// otherwise somewhat arbitrary.
    51	pub const min_window_width_cells: u32 = 10;
    52	pub const min_window_height_cells: u32 = 4;
    53	
    54	/// Minimum size in cells that the running program can resize the window
    55	/// to (CSI 8 t). This is larger than the minimum window size so that a
    56	/// program can't shrink the window to hide its output.
    57	const min_resize_width_cells: u32 = 40;
    58	const min_resize_height_cells: u32 = 10;
    59	
    60	/// The maximum number of key tables that can be active at any
    61	/// given time. `activate_key_table` calls after this are ignored.
    62	const max_active_key_tables = 8;
    63	
    64	/// Unique ID used to identify this surface for IPC purposes. It is
    65	/// exposed to the commands running in surfaces as the environment variable
    66	/// GHOSTTY_SURFACE_ID. It must not be zero as zero is used to incicate a null
    67	/// value when communicating an ID over DBus as DBus does not allow null/maybe
    68	/// values.
    69	id: u64,
    70	
    71	/// Allocator
    72	alloc: Allocator,
    73	
    74	/// The app that this surface is attached to.
    75	app: *App,
    76	
    77	/// The windowing system surface and app.
    78	rt_app: *apprt.runtime.App,
    79	rt_surface: *apprt.runtime.Surface,
    80	
    81	/// The font structures
    82	font_grid_key: font.SharedGridSet.Key,
    83	font_size: font.face.DesiredSize,
    84	font_metrics: font.Metrics,
    85	
    86	/// This keeps track of if the font size was ever modified. If it wasn't,
    87	/// then config reloading will change the font. If it was manually adjusted,
    88	/// we don't change it on config reload since we assume the user wants
    89	/// a specific size.
    90	font_size_adjusted: bool,
    91	
    92	/// The renderer for this surface.
    93	renderer: Renderer,
    94	
    95	/// The render state
    96	renderer_state: rendererpkg.State,
    97	
    98	/// The renderer thread manager
    99	renderer_thread: rendererpkg.Thread,
   100	
   101	/// The actual thread
   102	renderer_thr: std.Thread,
   103	
   104	/// Mouse state.
   105	mouse: Mouse,
   106	
   107	/// Keyboard input state.
   108	keyboard: Keyboard,
   109	
   110	/// A currently pressed key. This is used so that we can send a keyboard
   111	/// release event when the surface is unfocused. Note that when the surface
   112	/// is refocused, a key press event may not be sent again -- this depends
   113	/// on the apprt (UI framework) in use, but we want to consistently send
   114	/// a release.
   115	///
   116	/// This is only sent when a keypress event results in a key event being
   117	/// sent to the pty. If it is consumed by a keybinding or other action,
   118	/// this is not set.
   119	///
   120	/// Also note the utf8 value is not valid for this event so some unfocused
   121	/// release events may not send exactly the right data within Kitty keyboard
